Professional Positioning

Product Designer and UX Engineer focused on turning user and operational
problems into understandable digital experiences through interface
design, interaction design, prototyping, and frontend implementation.

The portfolio combines product-design work with software engineering
projects. Project descriptions distinguish design concepts, implemented
functionality, and measured outcomes where those details are available.

Featured Case Studies

1. KytchenPulse — Kitchen Display System Interface

-   Case study:
    https://portfolio-kohl-eta-36.vercel.app/work/kytchenpulse
-   Role: Freelance UI/UX Designer
-   Focus: Dashboard and workflow UI
-   Tools and methods: Figma, UI/UX design, workflow mapping,
    design-system exploration

Overview: KytchenPulse explores a restaurant and kitchen display
interface intended to help kitchen staff review orders, track
preparation stages, and notice operational alerts in a fast-paced
environment.

Design considerations: - Use a clear visual hierarchy for order and
preparation states. - Organize order information to support quick
scanning. - Explore station-based organization for different preparation
areas. - Consider touch-friendly controls for tablet use.

These are design considerations for the interface. Specific thresholds,
timing rules, usability results, and claims of operational improvement
should be included only where supported by project artifacts or testing.

2. UniRide — Campus Ride-Pooling Experience

-   Case study: https://portfolio-kohl-eta-36.vercel.app/work/uniride
-   Role: UX Engineer and Mobile Developer
-   Focus: Mobile UX and ride coordination
-   Technologies: React Native, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL,
    Supabase, WebSockets
-   Design tool: Figma, where applicable to the work shown

Overview: UniRide is a campus-focused ride-pooling application concept
and project intended to help university students find rides, request
seats, and coordinate with ride creators.

Design considerations: - Make ride discovery and seat availability easy
to understand. - Clarify the steps and status of a ride request. -
Provide a clear path to communication after a request is accepted. -
Communicate relevant ride and participant information clearly.

The project description should distinguish implemented features from
proposed UI concepts. Mapbox integration, measured sub-200ms updates,
and other performance claims should be stated only if verified in the
actual implementation and test results.

3. SRM Sports Council — Sports Management and Booking Workflows

-   Case study:
    https://portfolio-kohl-eta-36.vercel.app/work/sports-council
-   Role: UI/UX Designer and Full-Stack Developer, as applicable to the
    work presented
-   Focus: Registration, club workflows, slot booking, and
    administrative dashboards
-   Technologies: React, Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB

Overview: The SRM Sports Council Management Platform supports
sports-related workflows, including student and club registration, slot
booking, and administrative event or registration management.

Design considerations: - Separate student-facing tasks from
administrative tasks. - Make registration steps and approval status
understandable. - Present slot availability and booking status
clearly. - Provide clear validation, error, and confirmation states.

The project uses modular backend services for registration, club
registration, and slot-booking workflows where implemented. Claims about
booking speed, number of clicks, specific calendar behavior, or measured
usability improvements should be included only when verified.

Design Approach

The following is the general design approach used where appropriate. It
does not imply that every activity was performed for every project.

1.  Discover: Understand the context, requirements, users, and potential
    pain points. Use stakeholder discussions or competitive analysis
    when actually conducted.
2.  Define: Clarify the problem, user needs, task flows, and information
    structure.
3.  Explore: Compare layout options, navigation patterns, and
    low-fidelity wireframes.
4.  Prototype and evaluate: Create high-fidelity screens and interactive
    prototypes; evaluate usability when testing has been performed.
5.  Implement and refine: Translate designs into responsive interfaces,
    refine reusable components, and check accessibility and interaction
    states.

Case studies should show real artifacts and explain the design decisions
made. Clearly label retrospective design work, proposals, and untested
assumptions.

    portfolio and professional interests.
